tools.name: get_glossary_term
tools.description: Everything about one word of the Narrate glossary by its id (from search_glossary): the term in both languages, its definition per language level, the words to avoid, an example, the words not to confuse it with, and its source.

tools.name: search_pages
tools.description: Search the public pages of narrate.works (articles, guides, materials, the glossary) by title, description and full text. Returns paths to read with read_page, with a short fragment where the words occur in the text.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Reads one public page of narrate.works as Markdown, opening with that page's instructions for AI assistants (how to cite it, what not to say). Use a path from search_pages, e.g. '/naslag/begrippen' or '/reference/glossary'.

tools.name: search_sources
tools.description: Search the sources Narrate cites (reports, laws, standards, books, our own counts) by title, publisher or id. Returns ids to read with get_source. tools.name: get_source
tools.description: Everything public about one source by its id (from search_sources): title, publisher, date, URL, licence, the literal quote Narrate leans on and where it stands, whether it was checked three times, and whether something overtook it.

tools.name: search_keywords
tools.description: The keywords Narrate tags its work with, by group: perspectives, phases, challenges, sectors, organisational forms, frameworks, technology and product forms. Each keyword links to the page where it lives, to read with read_page.

tools.name: list_articles
tools.description: Narrate's published articles, newest first, as on narrate.works/materialen/artikelen (English /resources/articles). tools.name: get_status
tools.description: How Narrate's services stand right now (website, signing in, data, workspace: working, slow or disrupted), the notice that is open, and planned maintenance within a day. tools.name: list_specials
tools.description: The specials: Narrate's long, illustrated articles, with figures you can explore. Returns each with its title, description and path; read one in full with read_page.

tools.name: suggest_examples
tools.description: Narrate's example library: made-up initiatives that explain an idea in the reader's own world. Give an audience group, a challenge or a NACE section and get the best two to five, the ones the group would run itself first, spread over challenges. Every example is made up: say so, never present one as

tools.name: list_examples
tools.description: Every made-up example in Narrate's library that matches all given filters, in library order, each as a short card: situation, the change they want, the rights-holders, one figure and what is hard about it. No filter lists them all.

tools.name: get_example
tools.description: One made-up example by its id (from suggest_examples or list_examples): its card, the audience groups it serves and its tags.

tools.name: example_coverage
tools.description: Per audience group: how many made-up examples it has, how many the group would run itself and over how many challenges they spread, against the norm of the library. Also the totals per challenge and scale, and the groups still below the norm.

tools.name: get_audience_fields
tools.description: The societal challenges and sectors where Narrate did work for one audience group, taken only from the cases and clients its own page shows. A group without such proof gets an empty list. Name the group by its key ('municipalities') or the slug of its page ('gemeenten').

tools.name: suggest_change
tools.description: Hand Narrate's team a suggestion without an account: a correction to a page or a glossary word, a missing source, an idea. findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "public" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_sources, get_source, list_articles · Public sink: suggest_change, list_shop_catalog · Destructive: suggest_examples, example_coverage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_sources, get_source, list_articles · Public sink: suggest_change, list_shop_catalog · Destructive: suggest_examples, example_coverage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
